summary: Ubuntu workstation imaging fails after firmware update: NVIDIA DKMS module unsigned under Secure Boot
description: Issue summary: A freshly imaged developer workstation fails to boot the NVIDIA kernel modules after a recent vendor firmware (BIOS/UEFI) update. The OS boots, but GPU-accelerated processes (docker containers requiring NVidia drivers, CUDA workloads) fail due to kernel module load errors referencing UEFI Secure Boot signature verification. This began after imaging several P1 machines with the new firmware applied at staging desk. Impact: developer workflows relying on GPU acceleration are blocked; repro rate ~6/8 machines imaged with the new firmware build. This ticket captures triage steps, logs, and a temporary workaround while we update the imaging recipe and endpoint signing process.
impact: Multiple engineers unable to run CUDA-accelerated containers; CI jobs that route to these workstations are failing. Affects ~6 recently provisioned staging workstations; no customer-facing service impact.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use current imaging pipeline (PXE -> autoprov script v3.7.1) to install Ubuntu 22.04.4 on a ThinkPad P1 Gen 5 with firmware 2.34 applied.
2) Reboot into target OS; install nvidia-driver-535 from apt and DKMS builds run during install.
3) Attempt to run nvidia-smi or docker container with nvidia runtime -> kernel module load fails with signature error.
4) Check `dmesg` and `mokutil --sb-state` for Secure Boot status.
5) Repeat on a machine with older firmware 2.28 to observe the DKMS modules load successfully (control).
logs: dmesg excerpt: [    5.412345] NVRM: loading NVIDIA UNIX x86_64 Kernel Module 535.54.03
dmesg excerpt: [    5.412389] nvidia: module verification failed: signature and/or required key missing - tainting kernel
dmesg excerpt: [    5.412400] MODULE_SIG: Required key not available
journalctl excerpt: dkms: nvidia_535: building for kernel 6.2.0-100-generic failed with exit code 2
investigation_notes: 2026-02-12 10:15 Lina: Confirmed reproducible on 6/8 staging P1 machines imaged between 2026-02-10 and 2026-02-12. All affected devices have firmware 2.34. Unaffected devices are either older firmware (2.28) or were imaged prior to PXE pipeline update.
2026-02-12 11:02 Rajesh: Verified Secure Boot is enabled by default on 2.34. DKMS compiles produce .ko files but kernel rejects unsigned modules; mokutil shows no enrolled key for our DKMS shims.
2026-02-12 13:40 Rajesh: Tested manual shim-signed flow by enrolling a test MOK and rebooting; after enrolling, kernel accepted modules and containers ran. Confirms signing is root cause.

2026-02-13 09:10 Rajesh: Checked imaging pipeline: build artifacts for nvidia dkms are created on build host but signing step had a missing step due to a packaging race introduced in autoprov v3.7.1 (job runner cleanup removed /var/tmp/dkms-sign-artefacts before signing completes).

2026-02-14 16:20 SRE: Correlated with endpoint-management policy that enforces Secure Boot with vendor keys; need to add automated MOK enrollment or switch to fully signed shim per firmware requirements.
2026-02-15 10:05 Lina: Noted temporary workaround applied to two workstations by enrolling MOKs manually; documented commands below.
temporary_workaround: On affected machines, run: sudo apt install mokutil; sudo update-initramfs -u; use scripts/sign-dkms.sh to sign all /lib/modules/*/extra modules; sudo mokutil --import /etc/keys/dkms_mok.der; reboot and enroll MOK at UEFI prompt. This restores GPU functionality but requires manual steps and user presence at reboot.
resolution: Workaround validated for affected devices. Imaging pipeline change planned: fix race in autoprov v3.7.1 to ensure DKMS signing step completes; add automated MOK import step into preseed/ignition and update imaging runbook. Also opened follow-up task to coordinate with hardware (firmware vendor) and endpoint team to standardize shim signing so manual MOK enrollment is not required.
follow_up_tasks: INT-8040: Update PXE/autoprov job runner to remove premature cleanup and add explicit signing completion check
INT-8041: Coordinate with Endpoint team to add MOK enrollment to provisioning image or publish signed shim in approved keystore
INT-8042: Audit recent inventory for devices with firmware >=2.34 and flag for re-provisioning or manual MOK enrollment
comments: 2026-02-12 11:30 Rajesh Iyer: Initial triage - Secure Boot appears to be preventing unsigned DKMS modules from loading. Reproduced locally on test bench. Will attempt manual signing to confirm.
2026-02-12 13:55 Lina Park: Confirmed manual MOK enrollment restored GPU on RDWD-4729. Documented steps in runbook draft. Marking as P2 since workaround is manual.

2026-02-13 08:20 Nadia Chen (SRE): FYI, endpoint policy recently tightened Secure Boot acceptance; we need to coordinate before flipping MOK enrollment on fleet images. I've added a brief to the security channel.
2026-02-16 09:00 Rajesh Iyer: Patch submitted to autoprov to add a signing-complete wait and upload signed artifacts to artifact store. PR linked above. Scheduling image bake and test on 2026-02-18.
2026-02-18 16:30 Lina Park: Bake passed on 3 test machines with firmware 2.34. Will begin rolling to remaining staging devices. Closing after rollout verification and audit.
